findings.finding: Adult eight weeks after hemorrhagic stroke has functionally problematic dynamic plantarflexor overactivity: fast-stretch catch, MAS 2, clonus, toe drag, preserved slow dorsiflexion to neutral. This supports the focal PM&R impairment decision and lies within the early-intervention population; fixed contracture is not asserted.

Candidate A offers focal botulinum toxin for measured tone reduction without promising walking benefit. The early-intervention systematic review supports spasticity reduction within three months but cannot establish activity benefit; the VA/DoD synopsis includes botulinum toxin for spasticity. AFO is separately offered for mobility; its guideline explicitly advises against using it to decrease plantarflexor spasticity, making B substantively wrong. No unsupported dose, guaranteed functional improvement, or treatment ranking is introduced.

Actual blind_entry output examined. Neutral title and question, descriptive impairment findings, and no treatment recommendation in the chart. Private key, claims, keywords, hard hook, reasoning divergence and error tags are absent.

All eight retained source identities, abstracts and hashes and the sole retained licensed body (33551975, CC BY 4.0) exactly match the original reference-preflight artifact. Current primary PubMed pages independently confirm the two decisive early-BoNT and AFO source identities and conclusions.
